title: PHP 8.6: Optimized printf changes compile-time acceptance of discarded expressions
body:
### Description

## Summary

PHP 8.6.0RC4 changes whether certain expressions containing an unsupported `(unset)` cast are accepted during compilation, depending on whether a function call follows an optimized or ordinary compilation path.

This produces different results for direct `printf()` calls and dynamic calls. Some expressions accepted by PHP 8.5 are rejected by PHP 8.6, while other expressions previously rejected are now accepted.

## Minimal reproducer

```php
<?php
printf(true || (unset)$x);
```

**Actual behavior:**

- PHP 8.5.10: Compilation succeeds.
- PHP 8.6.0RC4: Compilation fails with:

```text
Fatal error: The (unset) cast is no longer supported
```

### Dynamic-call control

```php
<?php
$f = "printf";
$f(true || (unset)$x);
```

Both PHP 8.5.10 and PHP 8.6.0RC4 accept this during compilation.

### Opposite acceptance difference

```php
<?php
printf(false ? (unset)$x : "ok");
```

- PHP 8.5.10: Compilation fails with the unsupported `(unset)` cast diagnostic.
- PHP 8.6.0RC4: Compilation succeeds.

These results occur during compilation, without executing the examples.

## Expected behavior / clarification requested

Is optimization-specific traversal intended to change compile-time PHP source validity, or should optimized and ordinary calls enforce the same validity rules?

In particular, which behavior is intended for the logical short-circuit and conditional-expression examples above?

Related observations involve `sprintf()`, qualified and imported calls, named arguments, unpacking, partial function application, and constant initializers. These appear to follow different compilation paths, but the examples above demonstrate the central inconsistency.

## Affected versions

- PHP 8.5.10 — Windows x64
- PHP 8.6.0RC4 — Windows x64, NTS, VC2022
- PHP 8.6 source commit: `f23b4c222cebe33be93ee8ecaaa14390c5507a08`

The PHP 8.6 executable was built from the specified source commit.

Reproduce with:

```powershell
php -n -l example.php
```

CLI OPcache and JIT were disabled. This behaviour is related to compiler lowering and constant-expression traversal, not runtime optimization.

## Relevant implementation

- [[zend_compile_func_printf](https://github.com/php/php-src/blob/f23b4c222cebe33be93ee8ecaaa14390c5507a08/Zend/zend_compile.c#L5264)](https://github.com/php/php-src/blob/f23b4c222cebe33be93ee8ecaaa14390c5507a08/Zend/zend_compile.c#L5264)
- [[zend_compile_func_sprintf](https://github.com/php/php-src/blob/f23b4c222cebe33be93ee8ecaaa14390c5507a08/Zend/zend_compile.c#L5096)](https://github.com/php/php-src/blob/f23b4c222cebe33be93ee8ecaaa14390c5507a08/Zend/zend_compile.c#L5096)
- [[zend_eval_const_expr](https://github.com/php/php-src/blob/f23b4c222cebe33be93ee8ecaaa14390c5507a08/Zend/zend_compile.c#L12920)](https://github.com/php/php-src/blob/f23b4c222cebe33be93ee8ecaaa14390c5507a08/Zend/zend_compile.c#L12920)
- [[Related PR #19658](https://github.com/php/php-src/pull/19658)](https://github.com/php/php-src/pull/19658)

The optimized call compilation path appears to traverse constant expressions differently from ordinary call compilation.

I would appreciate clarification on whether these differences are intentional language behaviour or an unintended consequence of compilation optimization.
